READ FIRST

How this assignment works

  • Share your screen in your breakout room, so we can drop in where it's useful.
  • exercises/lab.md is the source of truth: every command, and a callout for each known trap. If a slide and lab.md disagree, follow lab.md (and tell us).
  • Pre-flight passed? You ran preflight/scripts/preflight.sh before the course. Changed something since? Re-run it from the repo root; --no-pull --skip-smoke makes it quick.
  • Troubleshooting: machine problems (Docker, Python too old, busy ports, gh scopes) are in preflight/troubleshooting.md. Lab problems (port 8088 taken, no CI on your fork, a PR stuck on Expected) are callouts in exercises/lab.md.
  • Try it without AI: get the toolbelt in your fingers; you'll steer AI far better afterwards.
Ask earlyStuck for more than a couple of minutes? Say so in the room. That's exactly what we're here for.

SETUP · 1

Boot the lab gateway

  1. Get the latest course version (from any folder of your clone): it replaces your main, here and on your fork, so no merge conflicts.
  2. Open your clone in VS Code and a terminal in it (Terminal › New Terminal). Run every command of this lab from that terminal, in the lab folder.
  3. Stop the Lab 02 gateway: both labs use port 8088.
  4. Copy the env file and run scripts/setup.sh. It waits for RUNNING and prints the URL and login.
  5. Open the gateway and log in with the .env credentials.
# latest course version on main, here and on your fork
#    (replaces your main: no merge conflicts)
git fetch https://github.com/Mustry-Academy/cicd-for-ignition.git main \
  && git checkout -f -B main FETCH_HEAD && git push -f origin main

# VS Code terminal, at the root of your clone
cd labs/03-github-actions

(cd ../02-branching-and-prs && scripts/teardown.sh)

cp .env.example .env
scripts/setup.sh        # boots one gateway, waits for RUNNING
# open http://localhost:8088

scripts/teardown.sh     # stops it again
Port 8088 taken by something else?Set GATEWAY_PORT=8090 in .env and re-run scripts/setup.sh.

Install the linters, pinned, in a Python 3.12 venv

macOS

python -V                    # Python 3.12.x, same as CI
PART 1 · 1-3

Seed the broken state and hunt every finding

  1. Run scripts/seed.sh. It plants at least one issue per tool, including a brittle broken binding, a runaway poll and a mis-named component in the Overview view.
  2. Run all five checks and write down every finding: what the tool flagged, in which file. Don't use git diff: it shows all seven answers at once.
  3. Spend the most time on iglint: two rules fire on one binding (the Kiln tile), plus a poll-rate and a naming finding. Work out why each rule exists before fixing anything.
# plant the seven bugs into your working tree
scripts/seed.sh

# optional: reload the gateway to see the broken view
docker compose restart

# run all five checks · note every finding + its file
yamllint -c .yamllint.yml .
shellcheck scripts/*.sh
actionlint -config-file .github/actionlint.yaml \
  ../../.github/workflows/lab03-*.yml
iglint check .
scripts/validate.sh

# start over any time, then re-seed
git restore . && rm -f ../../.github/workflows/lab03-example.yml
PART 1 · 4-7

Fix every finding, read the documented mute, reset the tree

  1. Fix every finding. Record what was flagged, why your fix is correct, which production bug it catches. The seeded lab03-example.yml: bump it to actions/checkout@v7, don't delete it.
  2. Re-run every linter until each is silent and scripts/validate.sh exits 0.
  3. Read a finding configured away, not fixed: the comment on line-length: disable in .yamllint.yml. Compose has legitimately long environment: lines; the reason is written down so a reviewer sees judgment. Nothing to change.
  4. Don't commit: the planted bugs were never committed, so there is nothing to commit. Reset the tree; git status shows it clean.
# 7: back to the committed state
git restore .
rm -f ../../.github/workflows/lab03-example.yml
git status   # nothing to commit, working tree clean

Part 2, solo in your fork: build lab03-ci.yml and require it on main

  1. Step 0 · Buildthe skeleton, then the validate and lint jobs

PART 2 · 0

Swap the finished workflow for a skeleton you complete yourself

  1. Run scripts/prepare-part2.sh. It moves the shipped workflow to .github/ci-reference.yml (your answer key for step 2) and writes a bare skeleton to .github/workflows/lab03-ci.yml at the repo root, the only place GitHub reads workflows.
  2. Commit, then fill in the TODOs yourself: don't copy the reference.
scripts/prepare-part2.sh
git add -A && git commit -m "chore: set aside reference workflow, scaffold lab03-ci.yml skeleton"

# by hand instead: the git mv, then type the skeleton
git mv ../../.github/workflows/lab03-ci.yml .github/ci-reference.yml
git commit -m "chore: set aside the reference workflow"
.github/workflows/lab03-ci.yml · the skeleton
name: Lab 03 · CI
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "labs/03-github-actions/**"
      - ".github/workflows/lab03-*.yml"
permissions:
  contents: read
defaults:
  run:
    working-directory: labs/03-github-actions
jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # TODO (step 0): set up Python 3.12, install the pinned tools
      # TODO (step 0): run each linter
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # TODO (step 0): run scripts/validate.sh
PART 2 · 0

Write the validate job and watch it run on a test PR

  1. validate first: it's gateway-free, one run: step. Add timeout-minutes: 5. The lint job keeps its TODOs for now.
  2. Commit on your local main, push the same commit as a throwaway branch, open a PR and watch the checks.
  3. Read the logs on the PR's Checks tab: each step is its own collapsible block. Then close the PR unmerged.
Why close it unmergedMerging would put a merge commit on GitHub's main that your local main lacks: step 1's git push origin main would be rejected as non-fast-forward.
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: scripts/validate.sh
# on your local main
git add -A && git commit -m "ci: validate job"
# a throwaway branch, same commit
git branch ci/first-run && git push -u origin ci/first-run
gh pr create --head ci/first-run --fill
# checks take a few seconds to register
sleep 15 && gh pr checks ci/first-run --watch
gh pr close ci/first-run --delete-branch   # close it unmerged
PART 2 · 0

Write the lint job: the Part 1 linters, now running in CI

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10   # this job installs tools: more headroom
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install yamllint==1.35.1 iglint==0.1.0
      - run: yamllint -c .yamllint.yml . ../../.github/workflows/lab03-*.yml
      - uses: raven-actions/actionlint@v2
        with:                             # a `uses:` step: repo-root-relative
          files: ".github/workflows/lab03-*.yml"
          flags: "-config-file labs/03-github-actions/.github/actionlint.yaml"
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends shellcheck
      - run: shellcheck scripts/*.sh
      - run: iglint check --output-format github .
  • Same pins and the same Python "3.12" as your venv.
  • actionlint is a uses: step: it isn't installed on ubuntu-latest, so run: actionlint fails with command not found. uses: steps ignore working-directory.
  • --output-format github turns every iglint finding into an annotation on the PR's changed lines.
  • timeout-minutes on every job: a hung job otherwise bills for up to 6 hours. Too tight and a slow apt mirror flakes the check.
  • Job ids are check names: the ruleset in step 1 matches lint and validate by name. Rename a job and the required check waits forever.
PART 2 · 1a

Push your workflow to main, then protect main with a ruleset

Where
Settings › Rules › Rulesets › New ruleset › New branch ruleset
Ruleset name
protect-main
Enforcement status
Active
Bypass list
empty (the rules apply to you too, as admin)
Target branches
Add target › Include default branch
  • Restrict deletions
  • Require a pull request before merging · Required approvals: 0: GitHub never lets you approve your own PR
  • Require status checks to pass · Add checks: lint and validate
  • Block force pushes
  • Everything else unticked · Restrict updates blocks PR merges too

Then click Create.

# first: your finished workflow on main (not protected yet)
git add -A && git commit -m "ci: lab03 workflow"
git push origin main
Delete it when you finish Lab 03Every lab shares your fork's main: while the ruleset is on, PRs of other labs wait for lint and validate too. Settings › Rules › Rulesets › protect-main › Delete ruleset.
PART 2 · 1b-1c

A direct push to main is rejected; a green PR merges

  1. Push straight to main: GitHub rejects it, even for you as admin. Then drop the rejected commit.
  2. Merge through a PR: a real change on a branch (reword the Overview's Subtitle text in its view.json), green lint and validate, merge. An empty commit starts no checks.
# 1b · direct push: rejected
git switch main
git commit --allow-empty -m "test: direct to main"
git push                     # rejected: GH013 Repository rule violations
git reset --hard origin/main # drop the rejected commit

# 1c · PR, green, merge
git switch -c fix/proper-route
# reword the Overview Subtitle's text in its view.json, then:
git commit -am "feat: reword overview subtitle"
git push -u origin fix/proper-route
gh pr create --fill
# checks take a few seconds to register
sleep 15 && gh pr checks --watch && gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
git switch main && git pull
PART 2 · 1d-2

See a red PR blocked, fix it, then compare your workflow with the reference

  1. Break it: on a branch, set the Clock's poll to now(250) by hand, commit, open a PR. lint goes red and gh pr merge refuses. Pre-commit hook installed? Commit with --no-verify.
  2. Fix it with now(1500), not the exact original value: a PR with no net change starts no checks. Don't re-run scripts/seed.sh for this.
  3. Compare: same jobs and step order as the reference. The reference also narrows paths:, runs on every push to main and ends lint with docker compose config -q.
# 1d · break it on purpose, then fix it
git switch -c fix/regression
# edit the Clock binding → now(250), then:
# (pre-commit hook installed? add --no-verify)
git commit -am "test: reintroduce a bug"
git push -u origin fix/regression
gh pr create --fill
sleep 15 && gh pr checks --watch   # lint fails, merge blocked
# edit the Clock binding → now(1500), then:
git commit -am "fix: poll the clock at 1500 ms" && git push
sleep 15 && gh pr checks --watch && gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
git switch main && git pull

# 2 · diff your workflow against the reference
git diff --no-index \
  .github/ci-reference.yml ../../.github/workflows/lab03-ci.yml

Part 3, back together: self-hosted runners

  1. Discussionwhich of your deploys would need a self-hosted runner, and why specifically
  2. Optional hands-onregister an ephemeral runner, route one job, tear it down
OPTIONAL · HANDS-ON 1

Register an ephemeral runner

  1. Prereqs: Docker running, gh logged in with admin on your fork.
  2. Mint a registration token and start the runner container.
  3. Confirm it registered: the logs print "Listening for Jobs" and it shows on Settings › Actions › Runners.
Only hereYour own fork, an ephemeral runner, a workflow_dispatch job, and a teardown at the end.
REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner)

RUNNER_TOKEN=$(gh api -X POST \
  "repos/$REPO/actions/runners/registration-token" --jq .token)

docker run -d --rm --name lab03-runner \
  -e REPO_URL="https://github.com/$REPO" \
  -e RUNNER_TOKEN="$RUNNER_TOKEN" \
  -e LABELS="self-hosted,local-lab03" \
  -e EPHEMERAL=true \
  myoung34/github-runner:latest

# wait for "Listening for Jobs", then Ctrl-C
# (the runner keeps running)
docker logs -f lab03-runner
OPTIONAL · HANDS-ON 2

Route one job to your runner, check where it ran, tear the runner down

  1. Note the container ID and dispatch the shipped lab03-runner-demo.yml. Nothing to write.
  2. It goes green. The run log says ran on <ID>: the same ID as docker ps.
  3. The container exits after its one job, and the runner drops off the Runners tab.
  4. Tear down: remove the container if it's still up, and check the Runners tab is empty. Remove a lingering "Offline" runner by hand.
docker ps --filter name=lab03-runner --format '{{.ID}}'
gh workflow run lab03-runner-demo.yml
sleep 5
RUN_ID=$(gh run list --workflow lab03-runner-demo.yml \
  --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')
gh run watch "$RUN_ID"
gh run view "$RUN_ID" --log | grep "ran on" | tail -1

# tear down: a no-op if it already exited
docker rm -f lab03-runner
OPTIONAL · 1

Stretch 1: block bad commits with pre-commit before they leave your machine

  1. Install the tool in your venv: uv pip install pre-commit. No pre-commit install: scripts/setup.sh already set core.hooksPath.
  2. Baseline run over the whole lab: clean after Part 1.
  3. Set the Clock binding to now(250), try to commit, and watch the iglint hook refuse the commit.
  4. Undo the bad change. Commit went through anyway? Check pre-commit --version (venv active) and that git config core.hooksPath prints scripts/git-hooks; if not, re-run scripts/setup.sh.
uv pip install pre-commit
git config core.hooksPath     # → scripts/git-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files --config .pre-commit-config.yaml

# edit the Clock binding → now(250), then:
git commit -am "test: should be blocked"
# iglint hook fails, commit refused
OPTIONAL · 2

Stretch 2: a Run button and a masked secret

  1. Add the manual Run button: workflow_dispatch: under on:, merged to main through a PR. The Actions tab grows a Run workflow button.
  2. Watch GitHub mask a secret in your fork: create EXAMPLE_SECRET, echo it in a step, read *** in the log. Delete the echo step afterwards.
# A: a manual Run button (add under on:)
  workflow_dispatch:

# B: a secret in YOUR fork
gh secret set EXAMPLE_SECRET --body "hunter2" \
  -R "$(gh repo set-default --view)"
#    then add a step, push, and read the log:
      - run: echo "leak? ${{ secrets.EXAMPLE_SECRET }}"
#    log prints: leak? ***

Lab 03 done: a red PR can no longer reach main

  • You hunted seven planted bugs with five tools and can say which linter catches which class of bug, the Ignition-specific ones included.
  • Your repo runs a two-job workflow with least privilege, and a ruleset on main rejected your direct push and blocked a red PR.
  • Bring to the wrap-up: which linter would have caught your team's last real bug, and one iglint rule you'd call overreach.
Before Lab 04Delete the protect-main ruleset on your fork (every lab shares main) and skim docs/self-hosted-runners.md. Lab 04 opens up the Ignition file structure and deploys project files to a gateway, on the CI you just built.
